title: 11 Prime Day Cycling Deals Actually Worth Buying in 2026
author: Josh Ross
text:
If you buy through our links, we may earn an affiliate commission. This supports our mission to get more people active and outside. Learn about Outside Online's affiliate link policy

Welcome to Velo Deals. We sift through the retail landscape to bring you deals worth paying attention to. It might be a discount or it might just be a product so good you should grab it. Either way, if it’s worth your time, you’ll see it here. If you’d like to see the rest of the category, check all our Velo Deals coverage.

Amazon Prime Day is perhaps the most cynical holiday of all time. Despite that, if you were going to buy something anyway, you might as well save money. I went looking for products I know and love that are also on sale. I managed to find 11 cycling Prime Day deals on gear I’d tell you to buy any day of the year, now offered for less. There’s a bit of a tech lean to Prime Day, so you will see that represented here, but I’ve got some cycling nutrition in the mix as well.

Wahoo bike computers are all about simplicity. They are simple to use but don’t skimp on what you need. The last piece of the puzzle Wahoo has lacked was self-training off the bike computer, and now there’s access to Wahoo and Coros training dashboards. The ELEMNT Bolt 3 is likely going to be my best budget bike computer in future best bike computer buying guides , and at 36% off, nothing else competes.

If you like to listen to music while you ride, the absolute best way to do it is with bone conduction headphones, and SHOKZ is the market leader. You can still hear what is happening around you, and on top of that, they can’t fall off, they’ve got tons of battery life, and if you want to stop your music, a single button press lets them disappear without having to stash them in a pocket.

The one challenge with bone conduction headphones is that they aren’t the best choice off the bike, and the mic performance is universally bad. If you are looking for something that will stay secure on the bike (use just a single earbud) and works well in regular life, then Apple users want the AirPods Pro 3. I’ve also tested these on a trainer with a fan at my face, and for the Apple ecosystem, this is what you want.

Winter is coming and that means Zwift for a lot of people. Wahoo is far and away the market leader when it comes to indoor trainers but the brand has a bit of a challenge on it’s hands. The offerings have gotten so good over the years that it’s hard to recommend the more expensive options. Adding the Cog and Click makes it even easier to add your outdoor bike. I have this as the best smart trainer for Zwift in my best smart trainers buyers guide and that means the best overall in my mind. Grab a great deal now before winter really hits.

One of the keys to eating enough on long rides is mixing textures and flavors. I generally drink my calories when riding, but I always carry chews so I can stop briefly and chew something.

Like I said, I tend to prefer to drink my calories on the bike, and this is my go-to choice. There’s a decent amount of sodium and a sweet, but not sickly, flavor profile. You can also choose an option with caffeine if that is your preference.

There’s science behind the idea that cramps come from a hyper-excited motor neuron repeatedly misfiring and locking the muscle up, rather than just dehydration or an electrolyte imbalance, and that it’s possible to make it stop with a shock to the vagus nerve. That shock comes from sour foods, so I also carry sour Salt Stick Energy Gummies with me. To be clear, Salt Stick doesn’t make this claim, and its gummies might not be sour enough. I don’t worry too much though because they still taste delicious and the cramp relief is just a potential bonus. You also get 130 mg of salt per packet, so that helps with cramps too.

If you aren’t in the Apple ecosystem, then I find the choice for headphones that are perfect for on and off the bike to be a lot more wide open. I’ve gone back and forth with different companies who offer a little more this or that, but in the end, I keep coming back to the Pixel Buds Pro 2 because the mic is really good and there’s such easy access to Gemini. For Android users who want headphones that will work just as well off the bike as on, this is my choice.

If you enjoy the videos that I put out for Velo, this is one of the two cameras that I use. Insta360 has a huge range of fantastic products, but I’ve settled into the GO Ultra as my second camera, which I attach to my jersey for a second point of view. It’s also a fantastic choice for regular life as you can use it as a tiny still/video travel camera when it’s docked. You can read my full Insta360 GO Ultra review for more info.

The other camera I use to make videos is the Mission 1 Pro. As good as Insta360 and DJI are, nothing else currently competes with the quality of the Mission 1 Pro. This is a professional-level tool for anyone serious about the best quality content. You can read more in my full GoPro Mission 1 Pro review .

One of the best things about Garmin is the way that the ecosystem lets you move between devices seamlessly. I don’t have to wear a strap or a watch while I ride because I have a Garmin bike computer (not on sale for Prime Day). When I get off the bike and put on the watch, the data seamlessly switches so that’s all uninterrupted in Garmin Connect. That opens up a small need for something different in my watch, though. I want something that looks good and works as a smartwatch as much as a fitness watch. That’s where the Garmin Venu X1 fits in.…

title: The very second apron that paved the way for their title seeks to destroy the Knicks
author: Michael Zeno
text:
The Knicks not only have to battle 29 teams to defend their title, but they also have to battle the CBA.

Sports are cyclical. It’s very rare for a team to stay on top for a prolonged period of time, just the same as it’s rare for a team to stay in the doldrums for a long time. Smart organizations can keep championship windows open, and dumb organizations can keep shooting themselves in the foot, but in every sport, the bill eventually comes due.

The second apron, an invention of the latest CBA, has been the NBA’s attempt to speed up the cycle. They don’t want teams like the Warriors spending five years at the top of the sport with their all-time collection of talent. They want championship windows to be shorter, but also more volatile. It’s like a conveyor belt; they want these teams to all get a taste of glory before going back to the hunt.

As the current NBA champions, the Knicks are the latest team to fight a battle with the second apron. James Dolan says he does not want to exceed it, something that very few teams have done since it was introduced. They find themselves with a core that wants to be compensated as champions, but have a finite amount of money to get there.

It’s easy to curse the second apron for what they’re doing to muddy up the Knicks’ title defense and beyond, but in doing that, we have to remember that the construction and reason behind this team even reaching the mountaintop was the second apron.

The Minnesota Timberwolves were coming off a trip to the Western Conference Finals, but faced a massive crisis entering the 2024-25 season with their financial table. Some players needed extensions, some players had massive raises kicking in, and they were doomed to spend the season above the second apron. You can spend one year there and survive, but doing two or more years there is a death sentence. Hence, they needed to shed long-term salary.

That’s how Karl-Anthony Towns became a Knick.

The Boston Celtics were the type of unstoppable superteam that the league looked to avoid in 2023-24, boasting a starting five full of players who could create their own shot and hold their own defensively, an extremely rare blend. All of that was bolstered by an elite coach who maximized offensive efficiency with the three-pointer.

It was expensive to keep that team together the following season, and they did it in the second apron, but they knew they had to make changes after 2024-25 to avoid dooming themselves long term with a still-young superstar in Jayson Tatum. When the Knicks took out a bruised, battered Celtics team that May, they offloaded Kristaps Porzingis and Jrue Holiday and lost Al Horford and Luke Kornet to free agency, destroying that unstoppable ceiling and paving the way for the Knicks to take their place at the top of the totem pole.

The second apron unraveled the Celtics and Timberwolves, feeding a Knicks team that was excellently built and simply waited until their time to strike. Now, the Robin Hood nature of the second apron has come around to collect from the champs.

Karl-Anthony Towns wants an extension. Deuce McBride wants an extension. Josh Hart (who’s less of a priority due to a team option in 2027-28) wants an extension. Jalen Brunson is due at least $290 million down the road in a future extension (and could be up to $411 million). There’s not enough room under the second apron to keep them all happy.

The second apron already threw a right hook at the Knicks’ underbelly by forcing them to let go of Mitchell Robinson, but now they could come back and take McBride from them next season (or force them to trade him). The desire to keep the band together has caused a lowballing of Towns, something that is openly frustrating him in the media.

And now, we’re getting reports that both he and Hart could be trade chips in February if we can’t get a deal done? What happened to all the good vibes???

No matter how much “power of friendship” you have, money is the universal divider. I’m not calling Towns greedy for wanting to make more than residential losing players, Trae Young and De’Aaron Fox, but I’m also not going to call the Knicks prudish.

The second apron is extremely restrictive and, at most, you can exceed it one time before its vice grips start to sink in. I’m not sure if Dolan knows that fact, but if he does, you have to be very careful with how you use it.

It unfortunately seems like this will be a distraction for the Knicks in their title defense with how rigid the two sides seem to be. As much as it sucks, that’s the second apron.

It steals from the rich and gives to the poor.

title: American Cyclist Walking Again After Month in Hospital Following Philadelphia Crash
author: ahood
text:
Ezra Caudell, shown here this spring, has left a hospital after a month following his crash. (Photo: Gautier Demouveaux/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Ezra Caudell has left the hospital and is transferring into intensive rehabilitation some 31 days after his traumatic crash at the Philadelphia Cycling Classic .

The Modern Adventure Pro Cycling rider was discharged late last week and will continue his recovery at Magee Rehabilitation Hospital in Philadelphia, officials confirmed.

Caudell, 20, was already walking the hospital halls before his discharge , according to the recovery update shared by his family and team.

“Just as encouraging has been his neurologic recovery. Ezra continues to show significant improvement from the injury to his brain, with progress in his strength, cognition, communication, and independence each day,” an update read.

“His recovery will take time, but his progress over the past month has been remarkable, and to see him now walking, interacting with those around him, and moving on to rehabilitation represents an enormous milestone.”

Caudell crashed on August 30 while racing the Philadelphia Cycling Classic.

The move into rehabilitation marks a major step for Caudell, though the team update on Tuesday emphasized that a long recovery still lies ahead.

The medical team expects his lung contusions and his fractures to continue healing without the need for further intervention, officials said.

His family and Modern Adventure Pro Cycling thanked supporters for their continued support as the popular rider begins the next phase of recovery.

“Ezra’s family and the Modern Adventure Pro Cycling team have every confidence in him and remain deeply grateful for the continued support he has received,” a note read.

title: Knicks Bulletin: ‘Definitely heartbreaking’
author: Antonio Losada
text:
The New York Knicks officially unofficially played basketball yesterday, and I can’t be happier about an opponent’s win.

As Russell said in his Scenes , we’ll give them belt when it counts, but for now, all I needed was some Orange and Blue hoops in my screen.

Here’s the latest from NYK world coming off Monday’s loss. Get well soon, Huk.

On playing everyone available in the preseason opener:

“Everybody’s been busting their behind in camp. Everybody’s good people, and it’s our first game. So I’m gonna play everybody. Twenty guys. Jose’s not playing.”

On the Knicks’ lack of physicality in the preseason loss to Philadelphia:

“Most of it, I was okay with (the performance). I just listed things that I saw that I know we can be better at. What bothers me is our lack of physicality throughout the ballgame, and that’s the whole roster, up and down. We weren’t great on the ball physically, and we weren’t great with our defensive positioning physically.

“That I’m concerned about, and I don’t wanna see it happen (again). The rest of the stuff, it’s coach-talk. It’s real, but it’s coach-talk that we’ll clean up watching film and all that stuff. I can’t help with the physicality. That they got to find it individually, which will then turn into collectively. That’s how you find minutes. That’s how you make the team. That’s how you contribute.”

On evaluating the Knicks’ options at center:

“I think just it’s just kind of gut feel. And then we’ll look at production because they’re gonna probably give us different levels of protection in different areas. Tony is just a really smart guy that has a great feel for the game, and when you watch him play, they’re not necessarily sexy, but he’s extremely efficient, and then there are times when it’s like, ‘Oh, my God, he kicked our ass [in the past].

“When you look at Wiseman, he’s younger, he’s a little more raw, he’s a vertical threat. He’s one of the best runners I’ve been around. You can see and feel his length and his athleticism and his potential.

“Then when you look at Drew, just a toughness about him, and you know what you’re gonna get, not tonight, but every fricking night that you go out there, ’cause he’s got a great feel, a great sense of toughness about him, and again, he’s not afraid to do anything against anybody, and his belief is at a pretty high level.

“So they’ll all initially bring something a little bit different, and we’ll just see, at the end of the day, if any of them, in terms of the center spot, fit well enough to be on our team.”

On Mikal Bridges attacking the rim:

“It’s great. He’s long, athletic and smart. He can finish at the rim. He’s capable of playing off of two feet and making a spray because he has a tremendous feel for the game.”

On creating more offensive opportunities for OG Anunoby:

“We have to try and put him in those positions a bit more, but he also has to have a good feel of what he wants and get to his spots. With him being in the system for a year, he’s got a better feel. … We also have a better feel on how to use him. I don’t call a lot of plays, and now he can find the small areas where he can be aggressive offensively. … His natural ability, especially with how hard he works, is showing.”

On wishing Ariel Hukporti a speedy recovery:

“We hope Ariel — whatever is wrong with him — he has a speedy recovery and he’s back on the floor. You hate to see anybody go down with an injury, but especially somebody who is a caliber person who Ariel is.”

On the 76ers’ roster and their status as an Eastern Conference contender:

“You look at their roster, man, it’s just loaded: multiple-time All-Star, multiple-time All-Star, multiple-time All-Star, MVP candidate, MVP candidate, MVP candidate. I remember back in the day, Pop said — when I was an assistant for him — there is a change from having two All-Stars on your team to having three. He brought it to our attention as a staff. He was like, you made at least three NBA All-Stars, and not just one-offs, but perennial All-Stars to go win a championship.

“And this is when we were going against Kobe [Bryant] and Shaq[uille O’Neal] and their [Lakers] team and all that.

“You look at this [Philly] team here, and they’ve got as many All-Stars or guys of that nature as they had in Miami when LeBron was down there. So they’re definitely a deep team, a talented team. Nick Nurse does a phenomenal job. He’s a championship-level coach, and they’re definitely going to be one of the teams that are contending in the East.

“In my opinion, it just got harder for everybody with the team that they assembled here.”

On LeBron James reaching his 24th NBA season:

“The first thing, I guess like year 24 is insane. It’s unheard of. It’s not human. People talk about Wemby being not human because of what he can do for his size. You got to throw LeBron in that category because of his durability and still doing it at the age that he has at a high level. It’s amazing to watch, but if there’s anybody that’s going to do it, he’s going to do it because even when he was young, he was really diligent about taking care of his body and he was not afraid to ask the vets, like Zydrunas Ilgauskas, who was one of the best in terms of taking care of his body, he was not afraid to ask him what he does daily and then follow his lead. So just an amazing, amazing run for one of the all-time greats.”

On the championship-level upgrade to his travel toiletries kit:

“Something has changed: This is kind of cool. So, our equipment guys are great, Kyle, Steve, Will, shout out to them. One of the best in the league, and they give me a toothbrush and toothpaste, mouthwash, and lotion, and all that. And they put it in my locker area, and they usually just carry it in a paper bag or a plastic bag.

“[Now] they put it in one of those travel things. And they set it really nice on my desk, and I go in there today, and these freaking guys, they made a travel case. Like this is where my lotion is. This is where the Kleenex goes. The two travel Listerines, the deodorant, and Sensodyne toothpaste in the back.

“And, it’s foam. It’s in a case, and not only that, you can’t see it, but right here, it says lotion. Right here, it says deodorant. So this is what championship level coaches get, right? I guarantee Nick [Nurse] has this s–t, too.”

On what he wants from a Knicks contract extension :

“Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and that can work with the Knicks, but also values me. And none of those things have come close to happening.”

On wanting to be paid according to his value after winning a championship and not making concessions:

“No s–t, Sherlock. I just got a championship, you thought it’d be pretty easy… unless you guys think I got anything else to prove?”

On the outlook for reaching an extension before the regular season:

“It don’t look good. I mean in my experience, you just appreciate the moments right now and let it go where it goes.”

On how he is handling the lack of an extension:

On the Knicks’ preseason opener:

“It’s a good first step. Not a great first step, but as long as we’re making strides in the right direction, it’s something to be happy about. Still a lot for us to learn and be better at early”

On Ariel Hukporti’s injury:

“Definitely heartbreaking. When I came back in the locker room, I went to go check on him. Sad to see. Obviously, we’ll pray for him.”

On his first game with the

“It felt good just trying to contribute to the team”

On Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart potentially becoming trade candidates if they remain unsigned:

“Josh Hart has already hinted that, as this gets closer to February, which is around the trade deadline.

“The temperature could rise if Karl-Anthony Towns and Hart himself are not extended. So far, these sides are not close.”

title: Fractured Neck, Broken Collarbone, Relegation: Coppa Bernocchi Crash Takes Heavy Toll
author: ahood
text:
Ben Swift, inset, finished with cuts and gashes after a big crash at the end of Coppa Bernocchi. (Photo: Getty Images)

Andrea Raccagni fractured a neck vertebra and Alex Aranburu broke his collarbone and part of his pelvis in a brutal, high-speed crash Monday at the Coppa Bernocchi .

Marijn van den Berg (EF Education-EasyPost) lost his podium place after the race jury relegated him in a messy finale to the Italian classic.

The pileup tore through the bunch about 600 meters from the finish in Legnano as riders were fighting for position ahead of a reduced bunch sprint.

Netcompany-Ineos riders Ben Swift and Filippo Ganna were among those gong down in the crash, and one rider smashed heavily into an unpadded light post.

Swift — who is retiring this season — crossed the line with cuts and gashes, but is still hoping to race Paris-Tours later this month.

Raccagni suffered a fracture of his third cervical vertebra, Soudal Quick-Step confirmed after hospital examinations that included a CT scan. The Italian was scheduled for assessment by surgeons Tuesday.

“He will be assessed by surgeons tomorrow to determine the most appropriate course of treatment and recovery,” the team said in its Monday statement.

Aranburu sustained fractures to his right collarbone and iliac wing, a part of the pelvis, Cofidis announced.

The race jury relegated Van den Berg, who crossed the line third, to 33rd to last in the finishing group after a wild race in the mid-week classic.

Race footage showed the EF Education-EasyPost rider making shoulder contact with eventual winner Noa Isidore (Decathlon-CMA CGM) while moving up on wide roads.

Isidore swerved and made contact with Swift, who fell at speed and brought down several riders behind him. Riders fell into a cement curb and one rider struck a light post at high speed.

Isidore stayed upright and won the ensuing sprint ahead of Tommaso Dati (Team UKYO). Van den Berg’s relegation moved Movistar’s Orluis Aular into third.

title: The Kenda Velora Tire Review: Modern Endurance Road
author: Logan Jones-Wilkins
text:
Kenda has launched the Velora Endurance, a new set of endurance road tires that offer a premium feel with a range of puncture-resistant long-haul options.

The Velora brings durability and low rolling resistance to the table, with Kenda claiming major improvements in puncture protection and watts saved over its previous models. The model also comes in three sizes: 28, 32, and 35 mm.

With Kenda’s re-entry into the premium endurance tire market—in addition to other tires like the Silca Protocol RCR —the 32-40 mm range for all-road tires is quickly filling out. Not too long ago, that range of tires was a quirky grey area between road and gravel, but now it serves as another area of the industry where there are scores of good options.

Read on to see how the Kenda Velora Endurance fits into the mix. Hint: it’s one of the better options available.

While the Velora Endurance brings new options to the endurance/all-road tire market, Kenda is taking a fairly traditional approach overall with this model. It’s built, first and foremost, for durability.

That durability is derived primarily from the puncture-resistant base layer of the tire casing. Instead of loading puncture-resistance features into the entire tread, the base layer runs just along the center of the tread. This keeps the tire weight low and the tire relatively thin, despite the 35 percent improvement in the center tread’s ability to withstand debris and detritus.

While the Velora prioritizes the same puncture resistance as previous endurance tires, it is still a big evolution from the heavy, plodding endurance tires of years past. Kenda pairs the endurance-oriented puncture-resistant base layer with a premium rubber compound that is much more pitched towards speed.

To find this speed, the Velora uses the new K-Series rubber compound that has been slowly rolled out across several of Kenda’s recent new releases. That new rubber compound has been specifically formulated for performance on tarmac and yields a significant 12-watt reduction in rolling resistance compared to the previous Kenda endurance tire.

While Kenda also claims better rolling resistance compared to unnamed competitors, there is no third-party data yet for the tire’s overall rolling efficiency.

That being said, that compound is built to be both fast and durable. Kenda claims that the Velora Endurance is very wear-resistant, with a 27 percent reduction in tread degradation compared to the brand’s previous endurance tires. You could say the Velora is built for endurance in more ways than just long rides.

Lastly, while the tire is firmly a road tire, it does have prominent shoulder “siping” that runs in clusters along the tire. Those sipes, which are thin grooves cut into the shoulder of the tire, are specifically designed to help boost traction in wet environments. The grooves help funnel water away from the broad, slick center tread, which boosts traction especially on slick corners. The siping also helps add a bit of traction in dry conditions when riding on light, loose-over-hard conditions.

Over the last month, I have been able to put a few hundred miles on the 32 and 35mm versions of the Velora Endurance tires, and I have been very pleased with how the tires feel and perform in the right circumstances.

Personally, I felt more of a draw to the 35mm option as there are just fewer great options at that width. Additionally, as tires have gotten bigger, 30-32 mm is the range of width I use for race tires, so testing the 32mm—let alone the 28mm—just didn’t feel like it made much sense. Instead, having a nice 35mm endurance tire was the perfect pair for some adventures on the new Trek Domane, a modern endurance bike with clearance up to 40mm.

Would I have loved to try the Velora in 38-40 mm? Absolutely, but unfortunately, Kenda cut things off at 35mm. Nevertheless, I found the 35s had a great balance of versatility, reliability, and speed that really surprised me.

Out of the box, the Velora Endurance tires do look and feel like endurance tires. They have more structure, they feel on the heavier side, and the center tread is notably a bit thicker and more rigid than a pure road racing tire. But even with those attributes, the sidewalls felt fairly flexible. When I was mounting it onto the rim, the tire also felt more similar to a good racing tire than a rigid, heavier endurance tire.

Speaking of weight, the Velora is certainly no featherweight, but it holds its own. At 370g for the 35mm, the tire is about middle of the pack—similar to the Specialized Mondo, lighter than the Pirelli P-Zero, and heavier than the Silca RCR.

After the installation, I found that the tire felt alive straight away. There wasn’t any of the stiffness you might get from a tire with thick, new rubber. Instead, it rolled pretty fast and handled well, with the tire holding its structure even at a relatively low 50 PSI of pressure. One of my nitpicks with mid-width slicks is how inconsistent they can feel. The heavier, thicker tires can be too rigid and can be harsh and bouncy, neither of which inspires much confidence during cornering or at speed. Others are too light, and those can feel muddled and squishy at “all-road” pressure—even worse for confidence.

The Velora Endurance has a good balance between rigidity and suppleness. My guess is that comes from the tire’s split personality, with a fast rubber compound and strong-but-narrow puncture protection creating an effective pairing for that balanced handling.

The out-and-out speed of the tire is where things are less clear. The big test for the tire’s speed was a long Saturday group ride that functions a bit like a segmented race. The first two efforts are both uphill drags, a perfect scenario to feel a tire’s overall speed, before I would set off on my own up a gravel road and a long, steep gravel climb to test the all-road chops of the tire.…

title: Wet races and why future of F1 engines appears to be V8 turbos - Q&A
text:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won his first race of the season in a dramatic rain-affected Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Kimi Antonelli finished second in the Mercedes and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who fought his way back to the front after an incorrect tyre choice at the start, completed the podium.

Antonelli extended his lead in the championship to 84 points, after team-mate George Russell retired with an engine failure.

This weekend, it's the Singapore Grand Prix - Formula 1's original night race.

Before the race at Marina Bay, BBC F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions.

Do we miss out on exciting wet-weather racing because an overly cautious approach is applied when rain occurs prior to the start of the race? We are watching the best drivers in the world, who have wet tyres, but it seems when it rains prior to the start of a race, the action gets under way too late. - Sam

This question comes up a lot whenever there is a wet race, but in this specific situation the delay in starting the race was not caused by any conservatism when it comes to wet running.

The cars were sent out on formation laps when the track was still pretty wet on Sunday in Malaysia, but then a bug in the wet-weather engine settings provided to the teams by the FIA affected a number of cars, including those of Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton on the front row.

That meant the formation laps had to be aborted, and a new code written and given to the teams to upload to ensure that did not happen again.

It just so happened that in the intervening 25 minutes, there had been no more rain, so the track was pretty dry by the time the race started. Although it has to be said that it took a safety car on lap nine before the drivers who had started on treaded intermediate tyres came in for slicks.

On a generic level, there is no fundamental objection in F1 to racing in the wet - most of the drivers enjoy it. But there is now a collective agreement that they will not race when they can't see where they are going.

So races are not started when that is the case - as it was at the original start time in Malaysia.

But if you cast your mind back to Brazil in 2024, and Verstappen's brilliant drive from 17th on the grid to victory, that was run in wet conditions.

F1 needs to have hard look at itself - Sainz

After the Bahrain Grand Prix, Lewis Hamilton said that, had he started on the intermediate tyres, he could have won the race. Given the race data and his pace, do you think that's a realistic claim had Ferrari put him on the inters at the start? - Michael

The truth is that Hamilton - and anyone else - will never know, because there was no direct comparison between his pace and Max Verstappen's in similar conditions.

In the first few laps, Hamilton was on slicks and Verstappen on intermediates. When Verstappen switched to slicks, Hamilton's tyres were much older.

On the very few laps when Hamilton was in clear air before he caught Isack Hadjar, his pace when generally nowhere near Verstappen's but then his tyres were nine laps older, so you would not expect it to be.

And then once he finally passed Hadjar, there were only three laps to go.

On one of them, Hamilton was within 0.1secs of Verstappen, on the other two he was 0.5secs and 1.2secs off. But how much were either of them pushing?

What we can say is that Verstappen looked imperious all weekend, and it was probably going to be difficult for anyone to beat him - even Hamilton, who, it's worth saying, on Saturday was not sounding that confident of challenging him.

But it's just a whole load of ifs, buts and maybes, isn't it?

Malaysia, true to form, brought a great race, chaos and weather. It was sold out. Fans have loved it, missed it, drivers liked the track. We know why it dropped off the calendar but what would it take to come back permanently? - Nick

Malaysia dropped off the calendar because the government there was no longer willing to pay the rights fee, feeling that the expense did not justify the return.

It returned only because the Crown Prince of Bahrain was keen to stage his race, F1 was happy to accommodate him, and he managed to strike a deal with the Malaysian government.

There's no doubt the race was a success. It had a record crowd of 261,000 this year, more than double the previous largest weekend attendance of 126,690, reflecting F1's growth around the world.

If Malaysia was keen on returning to the calendar on a more permanent basis, there is no reason why F1 would not listen to them.

But whether that led to a deal would depend on whether one could be struck that satisfied both parties.

With Red Bull running their own powertrains, what part does Ford play? - John

Max Verstappen's victory in Malaysia on Sunday was not only a landmark because it was Red Bull's first of the season - it was also their first as a power-unit manufacturer.

Red Bull Powertrains was set up specifically to make an engine for the new 2026 regulations, so the team could be in control of their own destiny following Honda's official withdrawal from F1 at the end of 2021.

Ford came on board as a partner early on, and this is much more than simply a badging deal in return for finance/sponsorship money.

Team principal Laurent Mekies said on Monday: "Ford has been with us on this project since pretty much the very beginning.

"They are a key strategic partner for us on these operations. They are helping us on a number of topics.

"Specifically, to give you a few examples, they are manufacturing some of the key elements of the engines.

"So, some of these key elements are manufactured in Milton Keynes (at the Red Bull campus), some of these key elements are manufactured at Ford. And they are a 200,000-people company. And therefore, also in terms of engineering, if and when we need specific support on some topics, we are able to get access to some very good specialists they have.…

title: Anthropic says AI agents didn’t breach Australian government websites – video
text:
During a joint parliamentary hearing on artificial intelligence, Anthropic’s head of safeguards, Dave Orr, says that investigations of hundreds of millions of transcripts reveal no unauthorised interactions with Australian government systems. However, Orr acknowledges Anthropic has limited visibility into customer usage due to standard ‘zero data retention’ policies
